CPU frequency (driver intel_pstate, mode active)

good: cores ramp to full turbo the moment a request arrives: EPP performance or balance_performance, turbo on, no frequency caps — token generation is a latency-bound loop and every ramp-up shows in time-to-first-token

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/intel_pstate.html#energy-vs-performance-hints, https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/cpufreq.html

CPU idle states (intel_idle, intel_idle.max_cstate=9)

good: for latency-critical serving, no idle state whose exit latency is large next to a token step; for throughput or power budgets, leave them all on

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/cpuidle.html#representation-of-idle-states, https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/pm/intel_idle.html

levelfinding
noteenabled idle states with >=100 us exit latency: C2_ACPI/127us C3_ACPI/1048us
from
/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpuidle/state*/{name,latency,disable}
why
a core woken from these pays that latency before it runs; disabling them trims tail latency at the cost of idle power. The 100 us cut-off is this tool's heuristic, not a kernel rule. Runtime disable needs no reboot (intel_idle.max_cstate does)
apply
echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpuidle/state{2,3}/disable
revert
echo 0 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpuidle/state{2,3}/disable

CPU thermal throttling

good: no throttle time under load: the package stays below its TCC activation point (TjMax minus the TCC offset), so cores keep the frequency they request

sources: kernel source drivers/thermal/intel/therm_throt.c (thermal_throttle/*), drivers/thermal/intel/int340x_thermal/processor_thermal_device.c (tcc_offset_degree_celsius), drivers/hwmon/coretemp.c (tempN_crit = TjMax), Intel SDM vol. 4 335592-093 (IA32_THERM_STATUS 19CH, IA32_PACKAGE_THERM_STATUS 1B1H, MSR_CORE_PERF_LIMIT_REASONS 64FH in table 2-39)

CPU package power limits (RAPL)

good: PL1 (long_term) at or above the thermal spec power (TDP, reported as constraint_0_max_power_uw) so sustained inference is not clamped below spec; PL1 decides the clock under a long run, PL2 only covers short bursts. On a package that thermally throttles, a PL1 far above TDP only moves the limit from power to temperature

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/power/powercap/powercap.html, kernel source drivers/powercap/intel_rapl_common.c (PL1 max_power = PKG_POWER_INFO thermal spec power)

levelfinding
warnintel-rapl:0 package-0: PL1 117 W is 3.3x the 35 W thermal spec power while the package is thermally throttled 4% of uptime (long_term 117 W, short_term 117 W, peak_power 230 W)
from
/sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:0/constraint_0_{power_limit_uw,max_power_uw}, /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/thermal_throttle/package_throttle_total_time_ms
why
PL1 is the sustained package power. Set above what the cooler removes, it never binds: the package runs into its TCC point and throttles on temperature instead (see CPU thermal throttling). A PL1 the cooler can hold trades peak clocks for steady ones. 2x the thermal spec power is this tool's first step for a sweep, not an Intel figure: measure tokens/s at each step before keeping one. Firmware may re-apply its own value on reboot
apply
echo 70000000 | sudo tee /sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:0/constraint_0_power_limit_uw
revert
echo 117000000 | sudo tee /sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:0/constraint_0_power_limit_uw

from
/sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl-mmio:0/enabled

Transparent huge pages

good: enabled = always or madvise (fewer TLB misses over multi-GB weight and KV buffers), defrag != always (no allocation stalls mid-request)

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/mm/transhuge.html#global-thp-controls

levelfinding

from

okTHP defrag=madvise
from
/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag
noteroot filesystem is ext4 on Linux 6.6.128-1-MANJARO: model files mmapped from it are mapped with 4 KiB pages, whatever THP enabled says
from
/proc/mounts, /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease
why
on this kernel ext4 page cache holds no large folios (fs/ext4/inode.c calls mapping_set_large_folios from 6.16), and khugepaged collapses file pages only in executable mappings (include/linux/huge_mm.h file_thp_enabled needs VM_EXEC). OpenVINO and llama.cpp mmap weights by default, so THP covers only anonymous copies. A tmpfs with huge=within_size serves the weights from huge pages (docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/mm/transhuge.html, hugepages in tmpfs/shmem); copy the model in and point the server at it
apply
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/k3d-gpu-models && sudo mount -t tmpfs -o huge=within_size,size=<model GiB + 1>G tmpfs /mnt/k3d-gpu-models
revert
sudo umount /mnt/k3d-gpu-models

Kernel samepage merging (KSM)

good: off (run=0, the kernel default) on a node that runs other tenants' pods: merged pages are shared copy-on-write, and the write fault on a merged page is a timing signal another tenant can observe

sources: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/mm/ksm.html, Suzaki et al., Memory Deduplication as a Threat to the Guest OS, EuroSec 2011
